T0619.title: Disposal of Stolen Goods
T0619.definition: Disposal of stolen goods is the transfer and monetization of physical goods, virtual assets, accounts, or data obtained through fraud, theft, arbitrage, or other abusive behavior.
T0619.description:
Disposal of stolen goods sits at the monetization end of gray-market chains, often through second-hand platforms, offline dealers, recyclers, account brokers, virtual-gift recycling channels, or cross-platform trades. It converts assets obtained from low-price purchases, account theft, virtual-asset theft, malicious purchasing, and subsidy arbitrage into cash or reusable resources.

For risk governance, disposal clues can reveal upstream attack scale. For example, the same product batch flowing to a few addresses, similar accounts being resold by one broker, or virtual assets being sold at fixed discount channels usually indicates upstream bulk arbitrage or theft.
T0619.usageExample: Risk control traced second-hand resale clues backward and found that a batch of discounted goods came from bulk orders by one device cluster.
